consensus.title: Unit mismatch in watchdog timeout check

responses.content:
* [CRITICAL] [LOGIC] `elapsed` now returns milliseconds while callers still use a seconds threshold (`elapsed`)
  - Issue: The implementation changes the unit from seconds to milliseconds, but `check_stalled` still compares the result with `TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30` as though it were seconds. A job running for more than 30 milliseconds will therefore be cancelled as “timeout,” rather than after 30 seconds; conversely, the intended 30-second timeout is effectively reduced by a factor of 1000.
  - Fix: Keep `elapsed`’s seconds contract and return `time.monotonic() - started_at`, or update the timeout comparison to use `30_000` (and audit all other callers to use a consistent unit).

* [CRITICAL] LOGIC Unit mismatch in elapsed() function breaks timeout logic (at jobs/timing.py:elapsed)
  - Issue: The change from returning seconds to milliseconds creates a unit mismatch with TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30 in watchdog.py. Jobs will now be cancelled after 30 milliseconds instead of 30 seconds. The comparison `elapsed(job.started_at) > TIMEOUT_SECONDS` expects seconds but receives milliseconds, causing jobs to be cancelled ~1000x earlier than intended.
  - Fix: Either revert to returning seconds, or update the comparison in watchdog.py to `elapsed(job.started_at) > TIMEOUT_SECONDS * 1000` and rename the constant to TIMEOUT_MILLISECONDS.

[CRITICAL] LOGIC Unit mismatch in watchdog timeout check (at jobs/watchdog.py:check_stalled)
- Issue: The `elapsed` function now returns milliseconds, but `TIMEOUT_SECONDS` remains in seconds. The comparison `elapsed(job.started_at) > TIMEOUT_SECONDS` therefore triggers after ~30 ms instead of the intended 30 seconds, causing premature job cancellations.
- Fix: Convert the constant to milliseconds in the comparison: `if job.running and elapsed(job.started_at) > TIMEOUT_SECONDS * 1000:`.

[CRITICAL] LOGIC Premature job timeout due to elapsed returning milliseconds (at elapsed)
    - Issue: The elapsed function now returns milliseconds, but watchdog.py compares the result against TIMEOUT_SECONDS (30) assuming seconds, causing jobs to be cancelled after ~30 ms instead of 30 s.
    - Fix: Remove the *1000 factor and restore the docstring to indicate seconds.
